title: Prompts become numbers: tokens and embeddings

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the primary function of the embedding matrix E in the text encoding process?
options: To convert the text string into a sequence of integers
To map each token index to a vector representing its semantic meaning
To denoise the initial noise into a final image
To pad the prompt to the maximum length
questions.answer: To map each token index to a vector representing its semantic meaning
questions.why: The lesson states in Stage 2 that 'The embedding for token i_k is the row E[i_k]' and defines the embedding as 'a vector... that represents the semantic "smell" of that token.'

questions.q: In the provided lab output, what was the calculated cosine similarity between the two different prompts 'the dog ran in park' and 'the sun sat on mat'?
questions.why: The lab section explicitly lists the result line: 'RESULT sim_different = -0.152111'.

questions.q: Which specific file in the ComfyUI codebase contains the implementation for the T5 text encoder?
questions.why: The 'In ComfyUI' section states: 'T5: comfy/text_encoders/t5.py implements T5 and T5Attention.'

questions.q: Why is it important to use a mask when mean-pooling padded prompts in real inference?
options: To ensure the model understands the order of the tokens
To prevent padding tokens from diluting the semantic vector of the actual prompt
To increase the embedding dimension to match the latent dimension
To convert sub-word units back into full words
questions.answer: To prevent padding tokens from diluting the semantic vector of the actual prompt
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section explains that 'The mask... ensures that padding tokens do not contribute to the mean-pooled vector. If you ignore masks, your prompt's "scent" will be diluted by the "scent" of nothing.'

questions.q: What is the difference between the embedding dimension and the latent dimension as described in the lesson?
questions.answer: The embedding dimension is the size of the text vector (e.g., 768 for CLIP), while the latent dimension is the size of the image noise (e.g., 4 for SD1.5).
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section explicitly distinguishes them: 'The embedding dimension... is the size of the text vector. The latent dimension... is the size of the image noise.'
